title: Copilot Studio: cost controls in the Microsoft 365 admin center
summary: Hold: the resource-based spending-policy path stops before the required Resources policy-scope choice. The opt-in default, consumption billing and roadmap details are supported; the Power Platform hard-stop description also needs the documented exception for agent flows.

claims.where: front matter: status; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap target is October CY2026, a month already past at the stated November writing date.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "October CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap gives no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: The roadmap release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant), without listing a government cloud.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The four product associations match the roadmap.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft 365", "Microsoft 365 admin center", "Microsoft Copilot Studio", "Microsoft Power Platform governance and administration"]

claims.claim: Microsoft plans Microsoft 365 admin center cost management for Copilot Studio while retaining Power Platform admin center cost management.
claims.quote: We’re expanding cost management for Microsoft Copilot Studio into the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Resource-based environment and agent policies are the first planned scopes.
claims.quote: Resource-based policies for environments and agents are the first planned scopes

claims.claim: Broader user and group policy support is planned for a later phase.
claims.quote: with broader user and group policy support planned for a later phase.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans cost data in cost management and the agent registry for Microsoft-platform AI services and agents, including Cowork and Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: this update will introduce cost data into cost management and agent registry for AI services and agents built on Microsoft platforms (e.g., Cowork, Microsoft Copilot Studio agents).

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationales
claims.claim: The new control is admin-opt-in: existing Power Platform configuration remains effective until an administrator creates a resource-based policy covering it.
claims.quote: To opt in, create a Microsoft 365 admin center resource-based spending policy. Until then, your existing Power Platform admin center configuration remains in effect.

claims.claim: Opting in requires no separate migration step.
claims.quote: No separate migration step is required.

claims.where: What's changing: second paragraph; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Specific resource policies select individual agents.
claims.quote: **Specific resource** | Individual agents that you select.

claims.claim: Resource collection policies cover supported usage in selected environments, including deployed apps and workflows.
claims.quote: **Resource collection** | All supported usage in the environments that you select, including apps and workflows deployed in those environments.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A policy permits either no monthly limit or a configured monthly spending limit.
claims.quote: Choose No limit or set a monthly spending limit for the policy.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A resource-based policy can have an optional per-agent limit.
claims.quote: You can also set a per-agent limit so that no single agent covered by the policy uses more than the amount you specify.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Policy setup includes configurable alert thresholds and recipients.
claims.quote: Configure alert thresholds and recipients as needed.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A policy can use the default billing method or an available override.
claims.quote: Use the default billing method or choose an available billing-method override.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; controls[1].note; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Power Platform capacity allocations no longer apply to resources covered by the Microsoft 365 resource-based policy.
claims.quote: For resources covered by the spending policy, Copilot Credit management moves to the Microsoft 365 admin center, replacing their Power Platform admin center capacity allocations and linked billing plans.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; controls[3].note; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Linked Power Platform billing plans no longer apply while the environment is managed by a Microsoft 365 resource-based policy.
claims.quote: Existing Power Platform capacity allocations and linked billing plans don't apply while spending for that environment is managed by a resource-based spending policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Removing an environment from a resource-based policy automatically resumes its applicable Power Platform policy.
claims.quote: If you remove an environment from a spending policy or delete the resource-based spending policy, the applicable Power Platform admin center policy resumes for that environment automatically.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Deleting the resource-based policy automatically resumes the applicable Power Platform configuration without additional setup.
claims.quote: The same fallback applies when you delete the Microsoft 365 admin center resource-based spending policy that covered it; no additional Power Platform setup is required.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Learn says to allow up to 12 minutes after linking an environment for the policy to apply.
claims.quote: After you link an environment to a Microsoft 365 spending policy, allow up to 12 minutes for the new policy to apply.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: A tenant-by-tenant availability schedule or completion date is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio resource-based spending policies rollout; read the roadmap record, Manage Copilot Studio costs, usage-based billing overview and setup. They describe the target and policy setup, not tenant rollout completion.

claims.where: What's changing: agent registry; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited Copilot Studio agent-registry integration page lists no cost field in its visible metadata.
claims.quote: Searched: agent registry cost metadata; opened Agent registry integration for Copilot Studio and read Visible metadata. Its basic, configuration and governance metadata lists contain no cost field.

claims.claim: The specific planned addition of cost data to Copilot Studio registry metadata is not documented by the cited integration page.
claims.quote: Searched: agent registry cost metadata. The Copilot Studio registry integration page omits cost metadata; a separate Agent 365 Business Analytics Agents page documents a Cost column in its analytics table, not a Copilot Studio registry-metadata addition.

claims.claim: The cost-management feature documents no new access to agent content.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio resource-based data access; read Manage Copilot Studio costs, setup and usage-based billing overview. These document spending, billing and consumption visibility, not new content-access permissions.

claims.claim: Consumption views break down usage by policy, user, group, agent, service and funding source.
claims.quote: Review consumption by spending policy, user, group, agent, service, and funding source.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: AI Reader and Global Reader are supported consumption reader roles without configuration permissions.
claims.quote: AI Reader, Global Reader, License Administrator, and other supported reader-based roles can view consumption dashboards and reports.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Global administrator and Billing administrator can set billing methods.
claims.quote: Global administrator and Billing administrator roles can add, select, and change billing methods, and set billing methods in policies.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: AI administrator and License administrator can edit spending policies and manage limits and alerts.
claims.quote: AI administrator and License administrator roles can edit spending policies, manage limits and alerts, and billing methods.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The setup page excludes AI administrator and License administrator from policy creation and uses Global administrator or Billing administrator for initial creation.
claims.quote: However, they can't create spending policies.

claims.claim: An existing Power Platform role does not itself grant the Microsoft 365 role needed for these policies.
claims.quote: an existing Power Platform role does not itself become a Microsoft 365 role.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not specify the covered agent's detailed runtime behavior at the resource-based limit.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio resource-based policy limit reached agent hard stop. Read the feature page's limits and hierarchy passages and capacity-management page; the former states no identity-policy fallback but does not describe the runtime response or hard-stop mechanism.

claims.claim: The Power Platform per-agent limit supports notifications and a hard stop that turns the agent off.
claims.quote: **Hard stop**: The agent is automatically turned off once it hits the defined limit. ... An agent's monthly limit doesn't stop the agent flows that the agent calls. Agent flows are billed and checked for capacity separately
claims.fix: After the hard-stop description, add: "An agent's monthly limit doesn't stop the agent flows it calls; those flows are billed and checked for capacity separately." Keep the existing warning that enforcement is not instantaneous.

claims.claim: Power Platform agent limits are not applied instantly.
claims.quote: Limits aren't applied instantly. An agent can continue to respond for some time after it reaches its limit

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: The references do not explicitly confirm that the Power Platform per-agent hard stop remains applicable to usage covered by a Microsoft 365 resource policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio resource-based policy limit reached agent hard stop. Opened Manage Copilot Studio costs and Manage Copilot Credits and capacity. They give Microsoft 365 controls precedence but do not confirm continued Power Platform hard-stop enforcement for covered usage.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Scope
claims.claim: Resource-based policies do not cover AI Builder features or the credits those features consume.
claims.quote: Resource-based policies created in the Microsoft 365 admin center don't apply to AI Builder features or the credits they consume.

claims.claim: AI Builder powers prompts used as tools, in topics and as agent-flow nodes.
claims.quote: AI Builder powers prompts used as tools, in topics, and as nodes in agent flows.

claims.where: Scope: Out of scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises against moving resources, agents, workflows or environments using AI Builder to these policies.
claims.quote: Don't move resources, agents, workflows or environments that use AI Builder to these policies.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: All environments applies the resource policy tenant-wide and replaces the existing Power Platform spending controls.
claims.quote: Selecting **All environments** applies the resource-based spending policy to every environment and replaces their existing Power Platform admin center spending controls.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Learn recommends starting with Specific environments.
claims.quote: Start with **Specific environments** to gradually transition spending management to the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 resource-policy controls take precedence over Power Platform controls for covered environment or agent usage.
claims.quote: If a spending policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center covers the environment or agent, its controls take precedence over the Power Platform admin center controls for that usage.

claims.claim: A resource-based policy takes precedence over an identity-based policy.
claims.quote: Within the Microsoft 365 admin center, a policy for the agent or its environment takes precedence over a policy for the person using the agent.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: When resource policies overlap, the one with the higher applicable per-agent limit applies.
claims.quote: If you have a resource-based **All-environments** policy and a **Specific resource** HR agent policy, the policy with the higher per-agent limit applies.

claims.claim: Overlapping policy limits are not added together.
claims.quote: Spending limits from overlapping policies aren't combined.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Power Platform Manage capacity indicates when a Microsoft 365 resource policy manages an environment's credits.
claims.quote: the **Manage capacity** experience indicates when Copilot Credits for an environment are managed by a Microsoft 365 admin center resource-based spending policy

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Manage agent displays a message when a policy covers an agent.
claims.quote: The **Manage agent** experience also displays a message when an agent is covered by a policy.

claims.claim: The feature page's Before you begin section specifies roles rather than a licence or price for the control.
claims.quote: Before creating a resource-based spending policy for Copilot Studio agents, ensure that you have the necessary roles in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate licence or charge for the cost-management control itself is stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio cost management control separate license price prerequisites. Read the feature page, usage-based billing setup and overview; these specify administrator roles and credit funding, not a separate control licence or charge.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The consumption licensing model describes governed usage metered in Copilot Credits, funded through pay-as-you-go, P3 or prepaid capacity.
claims.quote: Microsoft's usage-based billing model charges customers based on actual usage, measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: The variable cost rating is consistent with the documented Copilot Credits meter.
claims.quote: Microsoft's usage-based billing model charges customers based on actual usage, measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Credits are billed to the Azure subscription selected in the billing method.
claims.quote: Copilot credits are billed to the subscription that you select in the billing method.

claims.claim: Once credits for the selected subscription run out, usage continues on pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: When credits run out for that subscription, usage automatically continues on a pay-as-you-go basis.

claims.claim: Copilot Credit Pre-purchase Plan (P3) is layered on top of pay-as-you-go rather than being a separate billing option.
claims.quote: P3 is layered on top of pay‑as‑you‑go.

claims.claim: P3 can be purchased from Cost Management > Configuration or the Azure portal.
claims.quote: by selecting **Buy Pre-purchase Credits** on the **Cost Management > Configuration** page. You can also complete this step through the Azure portal.

claims.claim: When both prepaid packs and a P3 subscription are selected, the billing order is packs, then P3, then pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote:
Prepaid Capacity packs
- Copilot Credit Pre-purchase plan (P3)
- Pay-as-you-go billing

claims.claim: Prepaid capacity pack credits can support services managed in either admin center.
claims.quote: Prepaid Capacity pack credits can support services managed in either admin center.

claims.claim: Credits allocated to Power Platform environments reduce credits available to other services in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Credits allocated to environments in the Power Platform admin center reduce the credits available for other services in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Apps and workflows cannot be selected individually and instead need an environment policy.
claims.quote: Apps and workflows don't currently appear in the agent selector, so you can't select an individual app or workflow. To cover them, create a policy for the environment where they're deployed.

claims.claim: Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy is the complete path to the resource-based spending-policy control.
claims.quote: Enter a name for the policy, then select **Resources** as its scope.
claims.fix: Replace controls[0].ui.path and the corresponding rendered path with "Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy > Resources > Specific environments". The cited procedure requires choosing Resources before selecting the environment scope; Add spending policy alone does not select a resource-based policy.

claims.where: controls[0].api; controls[0].note; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No Microsoft Graph operation for resource-based environment or agent spending policies is documented in the references.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio resource-based spending policies Microsoft Graph API; cost-management resource spendingPolicy. Read the updated API overview and spendingPolicy search excerpts: allUsersSpendingPolicy and selectedGroupsSpendingPolicy are documented, not resource policy types.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Manage Copilot Credits reaches environment capacity allocation.
claims.quote: Under the **Copilot Studio** heading, select **Manage Copilot Credits** or **Manage sessions**.
claims.fix: For the documented heading-complete path, use "Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits" in controls[1].ui.path and the rendered row. The second Copilot Studio is the heading on the Summary page, not another navigation choice.

claims.claim: pac licensing update-allocations-by-environment updates environment allocations and enforcement rules.
claims.quote: (Preview) Update currency allocations and enforcement rules for an environment.
claims.fix: Make the existing command identify the target and setting: "pac licensing update-allocations-by-environment --environment-id <environment-id> --currency-allocations <JSON array>". The reference documents --currency-allocations as the allocations and enforcement-rule input.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Manage Agents reaches the agent monthly-limit management page.
claims.quote: On the **Summary** tab, select **Manage Agents**. The **Agents** page appears

claims.claim: These references do not document an API explicitly identified as the Copilot Studio monthly per-agent limit control.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio monthly per-agent limit API Power Platform licensing resource threshold; Copilot Studio per-agent API threshold. Read capacity management and pac licensing upsert-resource-threshold: generic resource thresholds are documented without a Copilot Studio monthly-agent mapping.

claims.claim: Licensing > Pay-as-you-go plans > New billing plan > Azure subscription is the Power Platform admin center route into Azure-backed billing-plan setup.
claims.quote:
select **Pay-as-you-go plans**. The **Billing plans** page is displayed.
3. Select **New billing plan**. The **New billing plan** pane is displayed.
4. Select **Azure subscription**.

claims.claim: pac licensing create-billing-policy creates a billing policy and add-billing-policy-environment links it using --billing-policy-id and a JSON-array --environment-ids value.
claims.quote: (Preview) Link billing policy ID with environments. ... `--billing-policy-id` ... The billing policy ID. ... `--environment-ids` ... Provide the value as a JSON array.

claims.claim: The cited Power Platform CLI licensing commands are Preview.
claims.quote: (Preview) Manage licensing, entitlements, capacity, billing policies, and allocations.

claims.claim: Environment admin, Power Platform admin, Global admin and Dynamics 365 admin can create Power Platform billing policies.
claims.quote: Environment admin | Yes | Yes, for billing policies the admin created. | Yes, for billing policies the admin created and for environments in which they're admins.

claims.claim: Billing setup requires Azure subscription permission to create resources and register providers, or assistance from someone with those permissions.
claims.quote: You need to have permissions to create new resources and register resource providers in the subscription—or have the ability to work with another user who has these permissions.

claims.claim: Environment admins can edit only billing policies they created and link only their own policies to environments they administer.
claims.quote: Yes, for billing policies the admin created. | Yes, for billing policies the admin created and for environments in which they're admins.

claims.where: Governance controls: first paragraph after table
claims.claim: An identity-based policy cannot be converted into a resource-based policy; a new resource-based policy is needed.
claims.quote: You can't convert an existing identity-based policy into a resource-based policy. To manage a resource or environment when you have only an identity-based policy, create a new resource-based policy.

claims.claim: The Graph overview documents all-user and selected-group policy types.
claims.quote: Scope a policy to every user in the tenant (`allUsersSpendingPolicy`) or to selected groups (`selectedGroupsSpendingPolicy`).

claims.claim: The Graph Cost Management APIs are beta, subject to change and unsupported in production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the `/beta` version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Power Platform CLI documents generic environment-resource threshold automation.
claims.quote:
pac licensing upsert-resource-threshold

(Preview) Create or update the resource threshold for an environment resource.

claims.claim: The feature page recommends AI Administrator for Power Platform or Dynamics 365 administrators managing policies and AI Reader for environment administrators viewing consumption.
claims.quote:
Power Platform Administrator or Dynamics 365 Administrator | AI Administrator | Manage spending policies.
| Environment Administrator | AI Reader | View consumption when needed.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist's role-assignment checks have corresponding controls-table coverage.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Separate policy creators, editors and consumption readers' and 'Agree who holds Global administrator or Billing administrator'. The table covers spending policies, capacity allocation, agent limits and billing plans, not role assignment.
claims.fix: Move the Before rollout advice about separating policy creators, editors and readers, and agreeing who holds Global administrator or Billing administrator, to Scope: Roles. Do not add a control row.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The checklist's consumption-monitoring check has corresponding controls-table coverage.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Review consumption by environment and agent in Cost Management and compare it with the limits set.' The controls table has no consumption-monitoring row.
claims.fix: Move 'Review consumption by environment and agent in Cost Management and compare it with the limits set' from the After rollout checklist to the explanatory Governance controls prose. Do not add a control row.
